title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 45
paragraphs: Such, I say, are the tales these two sides tell, and each produces as evidence the following facts. The Sybarites point to a sacred enclosure and temple beside the dried-up bed of the Crathis, which they say that Dorieus, after he had helped take the city, set up to Athena surnamed “of the Crathis”; and besides, they consider the very death of Dorieus to be very strong evidence, thinking that he perished because he had acted contrary to the oracle given him—for if he had not turned aside along the way and had kept on doing what he had been sent to do, he would have conquered the land of Eryx, and having conquered it would have become its possessor, and he and his army would not have perished. The Crotoniats, on the other hand, declare that many things were granted in the territory of Croton as special gifts to Callias the Elean, of which the descendants of Callias were still in possession down to my time, while nothing was granted to Dorieus or to his descendants. But if Dorieus had indeed helped in the war against Sybaris, they say, many times as much as was given to Callias would have been given to him. These are the proofs the two sides produce, and we may agree with whichever we find more credible.
